topics.title: Use AI tools to analyze and understand the world and to create and inspire ideas

subtopics.title: AI tools can be applied to produce novel creations and inspire creativity

outcomes.text: Develop and evaluate an AI-based solution to address a real-world objective.
Describe how AI can create novel outcomes by identifying patterns in data from the domain of interest.

topics.title: Evaluate the uses of AI

subtopics.title: Using AI tools requires evaluation of their results and assessment of their appropriateness for specific applications

outcomes.text: Explain the potential limitations of AI; for example, insufficient or inaccurate data inputs, inability of the system to recognize its own errors, and flaws in the underlying algorithms.
Evaluate the results produced by an AI tool before using it.
Discuss challenges and considerations of AI with respect to personal privacy.
Evaluate the implications of AI on job markets and its role in automation and productivity.
Recognize the importance and challenges of human oversight in AI decision-making.
Recognize the purpose and suitability of AI tools for achieving specific outcomes.

subtopics.title: The development of AI systems can create ethical and legal dilemmas that will need to be resolved

outcomes.text: Identify arguments regarding the dilemmas created by advances in artificial intelligence.
Explain why computational artifacts can be attributed to an AI system rather than its initial programmers.
Describe the "Turing Test" and its implications for distinguishing human and artificial intelligences.
Articulate arguments against "artificial intelligence" qualifying as "actual intelligence" and counterarguments that refute those specific arguments.

topics.title: Practice responsible, ethical, and safe use of computing technology and the Internet

subtopics.title: Digital citizenship involves multiple practices intended to promote safety, well-being respectful discourse, ethical use of information, and positive relationships

outcomes.text: Describe how active and passive social media use can lead to positive and negative feelings.
Identify research trends related to the health impact of screen time.
Brainstorm strategies for navigating challenging relationships in a digital environment.
Learn strategies for civil discourse in a digital environment and apply them to a scenario involving uncivil discourse.
Define "digital reputation," and identify examples of social media posts that can have a positive or negative effect.
Explain why you should ask permission before posting pictures or information about someone else.
Identify strategies for protecting their privacy, including opting out of specific features and analyzing app or website privacy policies and terms of service.
Define "misinformation" and explore the consequences of spreading misinformation online.
Explore examples of confirmation bias, particularly related to news and online information.
